items.title: Local low-rank models for turbulent combustion
items.summary: TDB-L-CUR reduces the computational cost of turbulent combustion simulations using localized low-rank approximations. The method combines unsupervised clustering, local manifold, sparse sampling, and CSP-based treatment of fast chemical modes.
items.caption: N₂O mass fraction: DNS (top) and TDB-L-CUR (bottom). Kim et al. (2026), Fig. 8.
items.alt: DNS and TDB-L-CUR predictions of nitrous oxide mass fraction at five time instants in a three-dimensional turbulent premixed flame.

items.title: Differential diffusion and ammonia–hydrogen ignition
items.summary: We use DNS of turbulent NH₃/H₂/N₂–air mixing layers to investigate how differential diffusion of hydrogen and turbulent mixing influence ignition. A tagged-ammonia approach distinguishes fuel-derived nitrogen and provides a proper measure of differential diffusion.
items.caption: Chemical explosive mode (top) and temperature (bottom), Reₜ = 400. Oh, Kim et al. (2026), Fig. 15.
items.alt: Chemical explosive mode and temperature fields at four times in a turbulent ammonia–hydrogen mixing layer.

items.title: Accelerating chemistry in OpenFOAM
items.summary: We extend TDB-L-CUR to operator-splitting reacting-flow simulations in OpenFOAM. The method performs stiff chemistry integration only at selected grid points and combines inexpensive reaction-rate evaluations with low-rank reconstruction to reduce the computational cost of detailed chemistry.
items.caption: Temporal evolution of the mass fraction of CO₂ for Case 1, predicted by baseline (top) and TDB-L-CUR (bottom).
items.alt: CO₂ mass fraction contours at six times from 0.04 to 0.24 ms, comparing baseline simulations (top row) with TDB-L-CUR (bottom row). Both show closely matching vortex structures that grow and merge over time, with SSIM values above 0.99 throughout.
